name: neutral-vs-equilibrium
title: Neutral vs equilibrium: do dispersal-drift and colonization-extinction predict the same macroecology?
question:
Hubbell's (2001) neutral theory and MacArthur & Wilson's (1967) equilibrium
theory derive island diversity from completely different mechanisms — neutral
dispersal-drift among ecologically equivalent individuals in a fixed-size local
community, versus per-species colonization/extinction rates set by area and
isolation. Do these two mechanisms nonetheless predict the SAME emergent
macroecology — specifically, do both produce a positive species-area
relationship S ∝ A^z, and what does the neutral local species-abundance
distribution look like?
hypothesis:
The neutral metacommunity (Hubbell 2001) holds a zero-sum local community of
J = area*density individuals evolving by J Moran death/replacement events per
generation, with immigration probability m = immigration_base/(1+distance) from
a shared pool of n_pool species. Larger islands sample and retain more species
before drift erodes them, so a positive species-area relationship must emerge
with NO colonization/extinction rate asymmetry at all — purely from drift plus
dispersal. Run alongside the MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium composite over the
same area gradient, both models should show a positive z, but by different
mechanisms and (potentially) with different slopes. The neutral local community
should also display the characteristic skewed, concave rank-abundance /
zero-sum-multinomial species-abundance distribution from drift alone.
objective:
Over a shared log-spaced area gradient (12 islands, isolation fixed) and an
8-seed ensemble, measure the emergent species-area slope z for BOTH the neutral
(hubbell2001unified) and equilibrium (MacArthur-Wilson) composites, confirm both
are positive, and render (a) the SAR overlay on log-log axes and (b) the neutral
species-abundance distribution for a representative island (rank-abundance curve
+ Preston octaves).
description:
This study adds Hubbell's (2001) *Unified Neutral Theory of Biodiversity and
Biogeography* (citekey hubbell2001unified) as a mechanistic counterpoint to the
already-reproduced MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model. The
NeutralMetacommunityProcess assumes strict ecological equivalence: every
individual has identical birth/death/dispersal rates, and local diversity is a
dynamic balance between demographic drift in a finite zero-sum community and
immigration from the metacommunity. The metacommunity is treated as a uniform
pool, so the skewed local species-abundance distribution that appears is a pure
dispersal-drift result. By driving both the neutral and the equilibrium
composites over an identical area gradient we test whether two unrelated
mechanisms converge on the same macroecological law (a positive SAR) — a classic
question in community ecology (neutral theory as a null model for niche-based
equilibrium theory).

expected_behavior.name: neutral-produces-sar
expected_behavior.en:
The neutral (dispersal-drift) metacommunity produces a clear positive
species-area relationship (fitted power-law slope z > 0.05) from drift and
dispersal alone, with no colonization/extinction rate asymmetry.
expected_behavior.rationale:
If richness is set by a drift-dispersal balance in a fixed-J local community,
larger J (larger area) must hold more species, so S must rise with A. A
positive z establishes that neutral theory alone reproduces the SAR.

expected_behavior.name: both-models-show-sar
expected_behavior.en:
Both mechanisms — neutral dispersal-drift AND MacArthur-Wilson
colonization-extinction — yield a positive species-area relationship over the
same area gradient (both z > 0.05).
expected_behavior.rationale:
The headline comparison: two unrelated mechanisms converging on the same
qualitative macroecological law means the SAR cannot by itself discriminate
between neutral and niche-based (equilibrium) explanations.

behavior_tests.name: neutral-produces-sar
behavior_tests.description: The neutral model's fitted species-area slope z must exceed 0.05.

provenance.note:
Measured z_neutral = 0.763 (12 islands log-spaced area 1-100, density 2
→ J 2-200, immigration_base 0.2, n_pool 64, 8-seed ensemble, 300
generations, tail 25%). 0.05 is a conservative floor for "clear positive
SAR"; the measured value is far above it.

behavior_tests.name: both-models-show-sar
behavior_tests.description: Both the neutral and the equilibrium model must show z > 0.05.

provenance.note:
Measured z_neutral = 0.763 and z_equilibrium = 0.126 over the identical
area gradient (MacArthur-Wilson composite, n_pool 60, colonization_base
0.02, extinction_base 0.012, area_exponent 0.25). Both exceed 0.05, so
both_sar = 1.0 (both-positive indicator).

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Reproducing MacArthur-Wilson first (mw-equilibrium-reproduction) licenses
using its composite as the equilibrium comparator here; establishing that the
neutral model independently produces a positive SAR closes the
neutral-vs-equilibrium comparison.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Neutral vs equilibrium SAR + neutral species-abundance distribution (12 islands, 8-seed ensemble)

conclusion:
Two mechanisms, one law. Hubbell's (2001) zero-sum neutral metacommunity
(hubbell2001unified) produces a clear positive species-area relationship —
fitted slope z_neutral = 0.763 over a log-spaced area gradient (J = 2-200
individuals) — from dispersal-drift alone, with no colonization/extinction rate
asymmetry. The already-reproduced MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model over the
identical gradient gives z_equilibrium = 0.126. Both are positive, so the SAR by
itself cannot discriminate neutral from niche-based equilibrium explanations —
the central caution of neutral theory as a null model. The two slopes do differ
markedly: the neutral SAR is far steeper here because the smallest islands carry
only J = 2-3 individuals and drift drives them nearly monospecific (S ≈ 1-2),
while the equilibrium model keeps even the smallest islands richer; the neutral
slope accordingly overshoots the empirical z ≈ 0.1-0.35 band at this density.
The neutral local community reproduces the expected skewed, concave
rank-abundance curve and an internal-mode Preston octave distribution on the
largest island (~46 species of J = 200), the zero-sum-multinomial signature of
drift under a uniform metacommunity.

both-models-show-sar.detail: neutral z=0.76 and equilibrium z=0.13, both > 0.05.

findings.statement: Hubbell neutral drift also produces a positive species-area relationship (z ~ 0.76 vs equilibrium z ~ 0.13), so the SAR alone cannot discriminate neutral drift from niche-based colonization/extinction - two unrelated mechanisms converge on the same qualitative law.
